item.description:

Feel free to call the library or email central@sonomalibrary.org with any questions. Book Club titles and dates are subject to change. For up to date information visit: sonomalibrary.org/bookclubs January 13 - Transcendent Kingdom by Yaa Gyasi February 10 - The Fox Wife by Yangsze Choo March 10 - A Fever in the Heartland by Timothy Egan April 14 - The Kamogawa Food Detectives by Hisashi Kashiwai May 12 - The Husbands by Holly Gramazio June 9 - The Anxious Generation by Jonathan Haidt July 14 - Roses, in the Mouth of a Lion by Bushra Rehman August 11 - Martyr! by Kaveh Akbar September 8 - Feeding Ghosts by Tessa Hulls October 13 - The Heaven & Earth Grocery Store by James McBride November 10 - The Measure by Nikki Erlick

item.title: California Native Creations Art Show — Thu Sep 10, 8:30 AM — Person Senior Wing
item.description:
**September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month.** On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.
The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:
· Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,
· Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,
· Henry Edward Frank, *Yurok/Kashaya Pomo*, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled *Mind Prison,*
· Digital artist Nicolas (Nico) Vargas, *Kashia Band of Pomo Indians*, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.
· plus Gl

item.title: Pomo Honoring Month show on KOWS 92.5 FM with local speakers — Thu Sep 10, 7:00 PM — KOWS 92.5 FM radio
item.description:
**Tune in Friday,** **Nov. 6, 7 p.m., on KOWS 92.5 FM radio,** for the 17th annual Pomo Honoring Month conversation with Rose Hammock, (*Pomo, Wailacki, & Maidu*, *Tribal Member, Round Valley Indian Tribes)*; Raymond Sanchez, (*Kashia Band of Pomo)*; Angelica Smith *(Board Chair, Ya-Ka-Ama; Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria)*, and Christine Cobaugh (*Pomo Project Board Member)*.
Topics include information about Ya-Ka-Ama, the native-owned land in Western Sonoma County. For more than 50 years, native people have come together there for ceremonies, teaching and tribal activities. Visit: ya-ka-ama.org.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: An Afternoon for Wild Cheetahs — Fri Sep 11, 3:00 PM — Redwood Empire Food Bank
item.description:
Hi,
I’m hoping the attached invitation/information can be shared. This Friday, September 11th the Redwood Empire Food Bank is working with Cheetah Outreach Trust to raise awareness and promote communities and carnivores with a South African food and wine tasting event. Conservation Manager, Deon Cilliers from South Africa, will also be speaking about the current state of wild cheetahs and what can be done to save the species. Tickets are $25 and there is limited capacity. There is also a silent auction and merchandise available. This is a not for profit event and all proceeds go directly to cheetah conservation.
Thank you,
Janet Rose-Hinostroza
619-995-6822
Advisor/Spokesperson for Cheetah Outreach Trust
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Saturday Drawing Club — Sat Sep 12, 12:00 PM — City Arts Gallery
item.description:
Solano County Arts Council invites you to hang out and draw. This is a weekly, free event, open to all!
After grabbing some fresh produce at the Farmer's Market around the corner, stop by to doodle and draw in a casual, fun, and supportive environment. All ages, all skill levels. Just a fun place to hang out, meet new people, and draw together!
Bring your own supplies if you can, limited supplies will be made available. Please no inks or paints. Children must be accompanied by parent or guardian.
The art gallery is open during drawing club and showcases local original art. The gallery is regularly open Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 10 am to 2 pm, except second Fridays when it's open from 5 pm to 9 pm for Vallejo Second Friday Artwalk. We hope you'll stop by!
Source: North Bay Bohemian

The event will take place on **\[Saturday of 2nd week, 11/19/2026\]** from **\[6:30PM\]** to **\[10:00PM\]** at **\[Vietnamese Martyrs Catholic Church, 2652 Stony Point Rd. Santa Rosa, CA 95407\]**. Admission to the festival is **\[Free /per person\]**, and all members of the public are warmly invited to attend.
Rooted in ancient harvest traditions, the Moon Festival honors community, gratitude, and togetherness. Attendees can look forward to an exciting lineup of events, including:
**\[Vietnamese food\]**

**\[Lanterns for kids\]**

item.title: USAF Commanders Jazz Ensemble — Tue Sep 22, 7:30 PM — The Raven Performing Arts Theater
item.description:
**Free admission, but ticket required**. Maximum 4 per person.
The ensemble is part of the **United States Air Force Band of the Golden West**, stationed in the San Francisco Bay Area at Travis Air Force Base, California. The only active duty Air Force band west of the Rockies, the Band of the Golden West is comprised of about 60 talented and versatile Airmen-musicians under the command of Captain Brian O’Donnell. While they honor legends like Duke Ellington, Count Basie, and Glenn Miller, they seamlessly transition into cool jazz, bebop, Latin rhythms, Broadway hits, and patriotic music. In addition to performing for civilian communities throughout the states of California, Washington, Oregon, Arizona, and Nevada, the band supports 13 Air Force Bases, 8 Air Force Reserve Wings, and 6 recruiting squadrons in over 250 annual performances for 1.5 million listeners.

item.title: Saturday Drawing Club — Sat Sep 26, 12:00 PM — City Arts Gallery
item.description:
Solano County Arts Council invites you to hang out and draw. This is a weekly, free event, open to all!
After grabbing some fresh produce at the Farmer's Market around the corner, stop by to doodle and draw in a casual, fun, and supportive environment. All ages, all skill levels. Just a fun place to hang out, meet new people, and draw together!
Bring your own supplies if you can, limited supplies will be made available. Please no inks or paints. Children must be accompanied by parent or guardian.
The art gallery is open during drawing club and showcases local original art. The gallery is regularly open Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 10 am to 2 pm, except second Fridays when it's open from 5 pm to 9 pm for Vallejo Second Friday Artwalk. We hope you'll stop by!
Source: North Bay Bohemian
